1  COMMON JUDGMENT
This is a common judgment passed in M.V.C. No.1455/2025 and M.V.C.No.1456/2025.
Both petitions are arising out of same accident, hence they are clubbed and common judgment is passed in both cases.

Both petitions are filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- and Rs.30,00,000/- respectively for the death in MVC No.1455/2025 and injuries in MVC No.1456/2025 in the road traffic accident with cost and interest from the date of petition till realization.

2. The brief facts of both petitions is that, on 09.02.2025 at about 2.40 pm one Kempagangaiah was riding Honda Activa Moped bearing Reg.No.KA-52-U-9540 along with pillion rider by name Chandrakala from Dobbaspete towards Nelamangala, at that time one KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-14-F-0107 came from Tumkur towards Bengaluru driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed against Honda Activa Moped Bearing Reg.No.KA-52-U-9540 and Kempagangaiah sustained grievous injuries all over the body and died on the spot.

That Post mortem of the deceased in MVC No.1455/2025 was conducted by the doctor of Govt.
hospital, Nelamangala, the dead body of the deceased was handed over to the petitioners.
The petitioners have conducted last rites as per their customs and have spent more than Rs.2,00,000/-.
That the deceased was the head of the family, aged about 62 years, doing agriculture and self occupation.
Due to the sudden demise of the deceased the petitioners are undergoing deep mental shock, pain and sufferings and put to great financial hardship.
4. That pillion rider Chandrakala was shifted to Siddhartha hospital at T-Begur and after first aid she was shifted to Sapthagiri hospital, Bengaluru and then she was shifted to ESI hospital.

That petitioner sustained closed femur shaft fracture right with laceration over medial aspect of right knee, injury to left leg, head injury, abrasion over legs, hands, chest, forehead and other parts of the body and she took treatment as inpatient at ESI Model hospital, Bengaluru.

That she has spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards medicine, conveyances and attendant charges etc.
5.
That she was hale and healthy and working in private factory and also doing agricultural work and earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
After the accident she could not do any work.
She has lost earning capacity and put to great financial hardship.
The accident is caused due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-14-F-0107.
The Nelamangala Traffic police have registered a case in Crime.No.48/2025.
Respondent is the R.C owner and internal (SCCH-12) 4 MVC. No.1455,1456/2025 insurer of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-14-F-0107 and liable to pay compensation to petitioners.
On all these grounds they prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- and Rs.30,00,000/- respectively with cost & interest in the above case.
6. On issuance of notice, respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement contending that petition is not maintainable either in in law or on facts.

2 the petition is disputed on the ground that accident has not taken place within the jurisdiction of this court.

That on 09.02.2025 KSRTC bus bearing no.KA-14F-0107 was operated on its schedule trip from Shivamogga to Bangalore, driven by its driver slowly, carefully on NH-48 by observing all traffic rules and regulations.
That on the date of time of accident, there was no negligence or involvement of the said KSRTC Bus.

That the said bus was coming from Tumakuru towards Bangalore in NH48 and proceeding near Siddartha Medical College, T.Begur village at that time,
rider of motor cycle suddenly entered the road along with a pillion rider through the center median of road in order to cross the highway from service road without observing the movement of vehicles.

At that time, a KSRTC driver was driving the said bus on left side, but in front of his bus one Mini bus was proceeding, the rider of the motor cycle who crossed the highway through the center median drive the same in high speed in rash and negligent manner and in the process of avoiding collusion with Mini bus he lost control over his motor cycle and dashed (SCCH-12) 5 MVC.
No.1455,1456/2025 against the right side of the bus and caused accident.
That the petitioners have suppressed the fact with regard to manner of accident.
8. That complaint copy, FIR and claim petition, reveal the manner of accident in different ways which are not matching each other.
Further photos taken at the time of accident reveals the dame of motor cycle which is not correlated with the allegation made in the complaint copy.
That the investigation officer falsely implicated and filed charge sheet against the driver of respondent colluding with petitioners.
That the compensation claimed is excessive.
The petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary parties.
Petitioner ought to have impleaded the owner and insurer of motor cycle bearing no.KA-52-U-9540 which is responsible for accident.
Age, occupation, income, and Loss of earning capacity of the petitioners are denied.
On all these grounds respondent prayed to dismiss the petition.

9. On the basis of above pleadings, following issues are framed:-
ISSUES IN MVC NO. 1455/2025 1.
Whether the respondent proves this court has no jurisdiction to entertain the above case?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the LR's of one Kempagangaiah and competent persons to file this petition?

3. Whether petitioners prove that on 09.02.2025 at about 2.40 PM, one Kempagangaiah was riding Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-U-9546 from Dabaspete towards Nelamangala on NH-48 infront of Sidhartha Medical Collage, one KSRTC (SCCH-12) 6 MVC. No.1455,1456/2025

Bus bearing Reg, No.KA-14-F-0107 came from Tumakuru towards Bengaluru in high speed and rash and negligent manner, dashed to the Honda Activa ridden by petitioner and caused accident, due to which Kempagangaiah sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot?

13. ISSUE NO.3 IN MVC NO.1455/2025 AND
ISSUE NO.2 IN 1456/2025 :
In this issue petitioners have to prove negligence on part of the KSRTC bus driver.
According to petitioners the bike rider Kempagangaiah was riding the two wheeler in cautious manner, but bus driver came in rash and negligent manner and hit the two wheeler.
To prove this fact, son of the deceased got examined as P.W.1 and petitioner herself who is injured in MVC No.1456/2025 is examined as P.W.2.

They have Chandrakala P N vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35953204/
5 reiterated petition averments in their chief examination.

They have relied upon FIR, first information, spot panchanama, spot sketch, vehicle seizure panchanama, inquest, P.M, IMV report,
statement of accused, wound certificate along with discharge summary which are produced in their evidence.

On perusal of those documents it can be seen that, 3 rd petitioner herein who is son of the deceased has given first information to Nelamangala police on the same day of the accident stating while his father was riding two wheeler along with pillion rider, aforesaid bus driver caused accident and action may be taken against him.
Police registered FIR in crime No.48/2025 against the aforesaid bus driver for the offence p/u/s 281, 125(a), 106 of BNS.
They have drawn spot panchanama on the next day i.e., on 10.02.2025 at the spot of accident, the place shown by 1st informant.
It shows that it was highway N.H-48 tar road having east-west direction, 30ft wide.
(SCCH-12) 10 MVC.
As per the spot sketch there is divider open at the spot of the accident.
Deceased was traveling from Dobbespet side towards Nelamangala.
As per the spot sketch on the left side edge of the road accident has taken place.
As per the post mortem report Kempagangaiah died due to injuries sustained in RTA and as petitioner the IMV report both the vehicles have sustained damages.
Charge sheet is filed against the bus driver for negligence.
In the cross examination of P.W.1 and 2 they have denied the negligence on part of deceased in riding the two wheeler.
But to prove the said fact, Asst.Traffic Superintendent of Shivamogga Dist is examined as R.W.1.

In her evidence affidavit she has stated that driver by name Eranna.N.Shabinakatti (charge sheeted driver of bus) was driver-cum-conductor of KSRTC,
Shivamogga Division for the past 8 years.
That he is expired and therefore she is giving evidence in support of KSRTC based on the documents available.
She has stated that, on the date and time of the accident one mini bus driver was proceeding in right lane and this KSRTC bus was moving in permissible left lane.

Beside the said mini bus, this motor cycle rider was riding and in order to take turn near right side, near divider the motor cycle rider urgently crossed the mini bus and suddenly came to the right side of the KSRTC bus and dashed to right side head light.

Due to the impact,
pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries, injured was shifted to hospital and there was no negligence on part of the bus driver.
In her cross examination she denied material suggestions made by the petitioners.
She has produced one sketch prepared by the department and also statement given by the driver-cum- conductor along with photographs of KSRTC bus.

On perusal of those documents it can be seen that, driver- cum-conductor has given letter to his authority on 10.02.2025 and mentioned the same aforesaid facts which are mentioned by R.W.1 in her chief examination.
The sketch produced by her at Ex.R.3 is contrary to sketch prepared by police at Ex.P.6.In
Ex .R.3
in the middle divider of the road the spot of accident is shown in Tumkuru-Bengaluru highway while in Ex.P.6 on the left side edge of the road spot of accident is shown.
Therefore, there is contrary sketch which creates doubt at the spot of the accident.
To know the exact picture IMV report along with the oral evidence of P.W.1 and 2 can be examined.
In the IMV report bus got damaged on front right side shape, bumper, headlight, indicator, right side body while the two wheeler sustained excessive damage on the front side.

If the sketch prepared Chandrakala P N vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35953204/
6 by police believed, as the accident is said to have been taken place on the left side of the road, the damage should have been on the left side of the bus.
But, it is on the right side.
That tallies with the case of respondent rather than the case of petitioners.
In that view of the matter considering the oral and documentary evidence, in the opinion of this court, deceased also contributed to the accident.

The time of accident being 2.40 in the afternoon there is no doubt as to visibility of vehicles,
certainly if deceased had been more cautious, accident (SCCH-12) 12 MVC. No.1455,1456/2025 could have been avoided.
In that view of matter I am of the opinion that contribution of the deceased is 20% and contribution of bus driver is 80% in the accident.
Accordingly this issue is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE NO.4 IN MVC No.1455/2025
: In light of above reasons, petitioners are entitled for compensation.
Respondent being Corporation, having internal insurance, is liable to pay compensation to petitioners to the portion of negligence of its bus driver.
In respect of age of deceased, petitioners have produced Aadhaar card at Ex.P.16 and D.L at Ex.P.22 which shows that his date of birth is 02.03.1962.
Accident took place on 09.02.2025.
Therefore, the age of the deceased is considered as 62 years at the time of accident.
It is stated that he was Agriculturist.
As no income proof is produced, notional income of Rs.17,000/- per month is considered as the accident has taken place in the year 2025.
Petitioners being wife and children of the deceased, their separate income having not been proved, all of them are considered as dependents on the deceased.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under;
19. Loss of dependency :
As per the Praney Sethi case future prospects of the deceased will have to be added to the monthly income.
In case of self employed 10% of the actual income has to be added to the monthly income to the age group between 50 to 60 years.
Age of the deceased in this case is 62 years hence no future prospects has to be added.
Deceased being married (SCCH-12) 13 MVC.
No.1455,1456/2025 having 3 dependents 1/3rd of his income shall be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Hence, the loss of dependency is calculated as Rs.11,334 X 12 months = Rs.1,36,008/- X 7 multiplier to the age group of 61-65 years = Rs.9,52,056 /-.
As such, loss of dependency of the petitioners due to the death of their family member is Rs.9,52,056/-.
20. Loss of love and affection:
Petitioners being L.R's of the deceased have lost the love and affection of their husband and father respectively due to his death in the accident.
Therefore, for loss of love and affection compensation has to be granted.

There is no hard and fast rule in respect of measuring love and affection but, in the opinion of this court if amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded for loss of love and affection, the interest of justice would be met.
Accordingly, amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded.
21. Loss of Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses:

As per the judgment in Praney Sethi's case, the quantum of compensation for Loss of Consortium is fixed @ Rs.40,000/- and loss of estate and funeral expenses is fixed @ Rs.15,000/- respectively and it is revisable at 10% every 3 years.
As Chandrakala P N vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35953204/

, accident being taken place in the year 2025, under the head of loss of estate Rs.18,150/-, for funeral expenses Rs.18,150/- and for loss of consortium Rs.48,400/- each to petitioner No.1 to 3 is awarded.

22. ISSUE No.3 IN MVC NO.1456/2025: In light of above reasons, petitioner is entitled for compensation.

He is not treated doctor.
As per his clinical examination and evidence, fracture of right femur is united with implants in situ and there is wasting of thigh muscle with restricted knee and hip joint movements.

In his evidence he has mentioned that he has examined the petitioner on 02.10.2025 for assessment of disability.
According to him she has physical disability of right lower limb @47% and whole body disability @ 16%.

Petitioner is said to be working in a private factory, in these circumstances, injury to her thigh may not allow her to sit or stand for long duration and hence in the opinion of this court the functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner is 15%.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced 18 medical bills at Ex.P.27.
She has paid amount of Rs.28,764/- towards medical expenses.
Those bills are disputed but no concrete evidence is laid to dispute the bills.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for Rs.28,764/- under this head.
(ii) Food and nourishment:
The petitioner was in hospital for 13 days as per discharge summary produced at Ex.P.25.
Considering the cost of living, food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.500/- is awarded, Rs.500/- x 13days = Rs.6,500/-it will meet the ends of justice.
(SCCH-12) 16 MVC. No.1455,1456/2025 (iii) Attendant charges
: Someone must have taken care of the petitioner during her treatment period.
Even if her own family member has taken care, their those days income is lost.

Hence,
attendant charges of Rs.6,500/- is awarded.
(iv) Loss of income during laid up period: Minimum 3 months is required to recover from injury.
Therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total 3 months including in patient period.
His loss of income during laid up period is Rs.51,000/-.
He is entitled to that amount as loss of income during laid up period.
(v) Conveyance charges:
It is stated that petitioner took treatment at ESIC and Saptagiri hospital.
She has spent money for conveyance for the purpose of treatment.
Considering the same, this court is of the opinion that amount of Rs.5,000/- shall be awarded as conveyance charges.
(vi) Loss of future income due to Disability : As per the findings given above, there is 15% functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner.

Hence, loss of future income due to disability is Rs.17,000/- income X 12 months X 15% disability X 15 multiplier to the age group of 36-40 which comes up to Rs.4,59,000/- compensation is awarded under this head.
(vii) For Future medical expenses: As per the evidence of doctor there is need for removal of implants.
Hence amount of Rs.25,000/- is awarded for future medical treatment.
(viii) For Pain and sufferings:
The petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
The records show that she underwent surgery.
She was in hospital and suffered pain and agony.

Therefore, for (SCCH-12)

opennyai_summary.facts:
That Post mortem of the deceased in MVC No.1455/2025 was conducted by the doctor of Govt.
hospital, Nelamangala, the dead body of the deceased was handed over to the petitioners.
The petitioners have conducted last rites as per their customs and have spent more than Rs.2,00,000/-.
That the deceased was the head of the family, aged about 62 years, doing agriculture and self occupation.
Due to the sudden demise of the deceased the petitioners are undergoing deep mental shock, pain and sufferings and put to great financial hardship.
4. That pillion rider Chandrakala was shifted to Siddhartha hospital at T-Begur and after first aid she was shifted to Sapthagiri hospital, Bengaluru and then she was shifted to ESI hospital.
After the accident she could not do any work.
She has lost earning capacity and put to great financial hardship.
The accident is caused due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-14-F-0107.
The Nelamangala Traffic police have registered a case in Crime.No.48/2025.
Respondent is the R.C owner and internal (SCCH-12) 4 MVC. No.1455,1456/2025 insurer of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-14-F-0107 and liable to pay compensation to petitioners.
That on 09.02.2025 KSRTC bus bearing no.KA-14F-0107 was operated on its schedule trip from Shivamogga to Bangalore, driven by its driver slowly, carefully on NH-48 by observing all traffic rules and regulations.
That on the date of time of accident, there was no negligence or involvement of the said KSRTC Bus.
At that time, a KSRTC driver was driving the said bus on left side, but in front of his bus one Mini bus was proceeding, the rider of the motor cycle who crossed the highway through the center median drive the same in high speed in rash and negligent manner and in the process of avoiding collusion with Mini bus he lost control over his motor cycle and dashed (SCCH-12) 5 MVC.
No.1455,1456/2025 against the right side of the bus and caused accident.
That the petitioners have suppressed the fact with regard to manner of accident.
That the investigation officer falsely implicated and filed charge sheet against the driver of respondent colluding with petitioners.
That the compensation claimed is excessive.
The petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary parties.
Petitioner ought to have impleaded the owner and insurer of motor cycle bearing no.KA-52-U-9540 which is responsible for accident.
Age, occupation, income, and Loss of earning capacity of the petitioners are denied.
On all these grounds respondent prayed to dismiss the petition.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the respondent proves this court has no jurisdiction to entertain the above case?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the LR's of one Kempagangaiah and competent persons to file this petition?
3. Whether petitioners prove that on 09.02.2025 at about 2.40 PM, one Kempagangaiah was riding Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-U-9546 from Dabaspete towards Nelamangala on NH-48 infront of Sidhartha Medical Collage, one KSRTC (SCCH-12) 6 MVC. No.1455,1456/2025
Bus bearing Reg, No.KA-14-F-0107 came from Tumakuru towards Bengaluru in high speed and rash and negligent manner, dashed to the Honda Activa ridden by petitioner and caused accident, due to which Kempagangaiah sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot?
Chandrakala P N vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35953204/
3 4.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so by whom and what is the quantum?
5 . What Order or Award?
(Note: Issue No.1 shall be treated as preliminary issue)
ISSUES IN MVC NO.1456/2025 1.
Whether the respondent proves this court has no jurisdiction to entertain the above case?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that on 09.02.2025 at about 2.40 PM petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-U-9540 from Dabaspete towards Nelamangala on NH-48 infront of Sidhartha Medical Collage, one KSRTC Bus bearing Reg, No.KA-14-F-0107 came from Tumakuru towards Bengaluru in high speed and rash and negligent manner, dashed to the Honda Activa in which petitioner was traveling and caused accident, due to which petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged?
3.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so by whom and what is the quantum?
4. What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The said issue is treated as preliminarily issue and answered by order dt.02.09.2025 by separate order holding that this tribunal has jurisdiction to entertain the above case.
In that light this preliminary issue is held as this tribunal has jurisdiction to entertain the above case.
Therefore, on the basis of I.D proofs, this court comes to the conclusion that petitioners are the L.Rs of deceased (SCCH-12) 9 MVC. No.1455,1456/2025 Kempagangaiah and competent persons to file the above petition.
Respondent being Corporation, having internal insurance, is liable to pay compensation to petitioners to the portion of negligence of its bus driver.
Petitioners being wife and children of the deceased, their separate income having not been proved, all of them are considered as dependents on the deceased.
The quantum of compensation is determined as under;
19. Loss of dependency :
In case of self employed 10% of the actual income has to be added to the monthly income to the age group between 50 to 60 years.
Petitioners being L.R's of the deceased have lost the love and affection of their husband and father respectively due to his death in the accident.
Therefore, for loss of love and affection compensation has to be granted.
There is no hard and fast rule in respect of measuring love and affection but, in the opinion of this court if amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded for loss of love and affection, the interest of justice would be met.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
She was in hospital and suffered pain and agony.
But in the present case, the on going through the evidence and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner there is no chance of loss of future prospect.
opennyai_summary.decision:
, accident being taken place in the year 2025, under the head of loss of estate Rs.18,150/-, for funeral expenses Rs.18,150/- and for loss of consortium Rs.48,400/- each to petitioner No.1 to 3 is awarded.
Therefore, I hold that the petitioners are entitled for a compensation of Rs.9,46,845/-.
Hence no compensation is awarded under this head.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,37,412/- in respect of injuries sustained by her in the Road traffic accident precisely under the following heads;
Sl Particulars of Heads In Rs.
i.
Medical expenses 28,764/-
ii. Food and nourishment 6,500/-
iii Attendant charges 6,500/-
Total Rs. 6,71,764/-
 Contributory negligence on part of (-)1,34,352/-
 petitioner side bike rider @ 20%
 Grand
As per the settled law, interest @ 6% from the date of petition till the date of deposit will have to be awarded.
Accordingly, I answer this Issue "Partly in Affirmative".
- In view of above reasons I proceed to pass following;
ORDER IN MVC NO.1455/2025
The petition filed by the petitioners u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.9,46,845/- with interest @ 6% pa from the date of petition till the date of payment.
Respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners and hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within one month from the date of this order.
(SCCH-12) 19 MVC. No.1455,1456/2025 On such deposit, petitioners are entitled to have apportionment in the ratio of 60:20:20 and entitled to have release of entire amount without making F.D.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.
ORDER IN MVC NO.1456/2025
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,37,412/- with interest @ 6% pa on the amount of Rs.5,12,412/- ( future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/- will not carry interest) from the date of petition till the date of payment.
Respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within one month from the date of this order.
On such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to have release of 50% and remaining 50% shall be kept in F.D in her name in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.
